entities.summary:
The Battle of Bosworth Field was the last significant battle of the Wars of the Roses, a dynastic struggle between the houses of Lancaster and York, and marked the end of the Plantagenet dynasty in England.

On August 22, 1485, King Richard III, the last Yorkist king, was defeated by Henry Tudor, a Welsh lord, who then became King Henry VII, the first Tudor king of England.

This battle had a profound impact on English history, leading to the Tudor dynasty's establishment and paving the way for the rise of the powerful Tudor family, including Henry VIII and Mary I.

The legacy of the Battle of Bosworth Field can be seen in the subsequent reigns of the Tudor and Stuart monarchs, who played a significant role in shaping England's history and culture.

Henry Tudor's victory at Bosworth Field ensures a lasting cultural footprint: 'The battle won was won with my own hands, for God's sake, and with the help of my allies.' - Henry Tudor, after the battle
